<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a189267454139de981fa30aa66a4d47a948de8ab` — the merge of head `bfe6c78aa6ca6b2a2c1bc2c430ffb83599188b11` into base `fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

git fetch origin a189267454139de981fa30aa66a4d47a948de8ab && git checkout a189267454139de981fa30aa66a4d47a948de8ab

Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-summary-update-lock.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-blank-typed-value-door.test.ts, packages/rest/src/import-summary-update-lock-34672.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-data-blank-typed-value.test.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-master-detail-related.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-enable-refresh.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-backfill.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/core.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts

Inputs read: card #34672 body and all 6 comments (triage 6939838658, claim 6943806073, follow-up 6943855383, route amendment 6943935029, surface amendment 6946301740, dev report 6947820885; the card carries no maintainer ruling and no earlier contract record); PR #34752 body, 7-file list, the 3 PR comments, and the net diff from merge-base 6091b645 to the head; the check-runs on the head. Check-runs: 59 listed, all completed, every conclusion success or skipped, none failed, none pending. The Dogfood Regression Gate shards are among the skipped ones on this head (see ③).

### ① Derived judgments

The one behavioural hunk is `updateStaticReadonlySubject` in `engine-top-level.ts`: the schema view every update-side static `readonly` pass judges now carries each `type === 'summary'` field as `readonly: true` (`summaryFieldsLockedOnUpdate`). I traced each consumer of that view at the head: the pre-hook hide pass (`engine-update.ts` 569-592), the by-id strip (1474), the predicate strip (1866), `staticReadonlyStoredView` (the `readonlyWhen` strips and `staticReadonlyStripTakes` in the master-detail settlement), and the `update`-mode preview (`engine-validate.ts` 313). No other caller of `stripReadonlyFields` reads this view; the two insert-side callers read `insertStaticReadonlySubject`, which this diff does not touch.

Accept-set changes, each a narrowing, for a summary field that does not declare `readonly: true` (one that does is unchanged):

- Engine `update` by id, any context without `isSystem: true`, a call with no context included: main stored the caller's value; the head drops the key before the driver and reports `{ reason: 'readonly' }` through `onFieldsDropped`. RIGHT, pinned (new engine test, by-id case; forced edit 1 below shows the no-context call).
- Engine `update` by predicate (`multi: true`): main stored it on every matched row; the head drops it from all rows and reports once. RIGHT, pinned.
- REST `PATCH /api/v1/data/:object/:id`: main answered 200 and stored it; the head answers 200, stores the rest, and names the field in `droppedFields`. RIGHT, pinned on SQLite.
- REST batch `operation: 'update'` and REST `updateMany`: main stored it; the head keeps the stored value. RIGHT, pinned by forced edit 2 (stored value only; `droppedFields` is not asserted on these two doors).
- Import `writeMode: 'update'`, dry run and commit: main reported ok and stored it; the head reports the row's `droppedFields` on both and stores the engine's value. RIGHT, pinned.
- `validate` with `mode: 'update'`: the preview reports the same drop. RIGHT, pinned.
- Under `strictReadonlyWrites`, by id and by predicate: main wrote; the head refuses the whole update, nothing written. The refusal is the ordinary one: the strip is the same `stripReadonlyFields` call with the same `strictReadonlyWrites` option, and the test reads `code` `ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED`, `fields`, `drops`, `operation: 'update'`, the shape any read-only field gets. RIGHT, pinned at the engine; no REST-level strict case is in the diff.
- By construction, not pinned here: every other door that reaches `engine.update` without `isSystem` takes the same strip, such as the update arm of an upsert import, a hook's or action's `ctx.api` update and a flow's update step.

What is kept, read in the code:

- System writes are exempt on every pass: the hide pass and both strips are gated on `!opCtx.context?.isSystem`, and `staticReadonlyStoredView` returns the payload untouched when the strip does not run. The roll-up recompute writes with `{ ...execCtx, isSystem: true }` plus `SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE_WRITE` (`engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts` 603, 675); the enable refresh and `backfillSummaryNulls` write with `{ isSystem: true }`; the seed loader writes every row under `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT`, system-elevated per its docblock. The lock never reads the marker, so no system writer depends on it. RIGHT.
- A value a hook assigns is kept: the strip skips a key in `hookWrittenKeys` and a key whose value is no longer the caller's. Generic strip behaviour, unchanged; no new pin for a hook-written summary.
- `preserveAudit` keeps a caller's summary value on update: `isPreservableUnderAudit` admits any field that is not `system: true`, so a historical import (`treatAsHistorical`, gated by `importControlOptOutRefusal`) in update mode still stores it. That is the declared contract of the `readonly` key, and a summary that declares `readonly: true` answers the same on main. See N1.
- Insert is unchanged: `insertStaticReadonlySubject` and the runtime-owned strip are untouched, `RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES` still holds only `autonumber`, and the new test pins that a person's create keeps a supplied summary value with no drop event. The PR body and the changeset both state it. TRUE in the code.

Public surface: `summaryFieldsLockedOnUpdate` is exported from the module `engine-top-level.ts` only. `engine.ts` does not re-export it and neither package entry (`index.ts`, `core.ts`) names it, so it is not a published export, and the changeset is right not to name it. No spec path, no schema, no new drop reason.

The two forced test edits, as evidence of the narrowing:

1. `engine-blank-typed-value-door.test.ts`, case "update by id and update by predicate": it used to assert that a blank sent for `f_summary` reached the driver as `null` on `update` and on `updateMany`, that is, the engine accepted a caller clearing a roll-up. It now asserts that neither driver call carries an `f_summary` key; every other typed column still lands `null`.
2. `rest-data-blank-typed-value.test.ts`, the PATCH, batch update and `updateMany` doors on SQLite: each used to assert a stored `null` in `f_summary` over the seeded 7. Each now asserts the stored 7 stays. The create, batch create and `createMany` assertions are unchanged and still store `null` for a blank summary.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/objectql`, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset. RIGHT.

- `none` holds: nothing a metadata author can write is added, refused or tightened, and `packages/spec` is not touched. The published spec already classes `summary` under `COMPUTED_VALUE_TYPES`, "Server-computed types: never client-written", and the docs page already called summary fields server-owned; the engine now enforces that on update. Main carries the same pattern as precedent (for example `.changeset/33922-install-local-namespace-gate.md`, an enforcement of an existing declaration declared `none`).
- Level: AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3, a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The changeset has the banner, the one-line fix (leave the field out, or write with `isSystem: true`) and exactly one ADR-0087 marker. `Check Changeset` is success on the head.
- `packages/rest` changes tests only and publishes nothing; no second package is owed.
- The changeset's account matches the code for the doors it names. Its two omissions are N1.

### ③ Boundary flags

Security-touching: yes
The diff changes a server-enforced write guard: which caller may store a value in a column.

- `open_questions` in the dev report: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, insert half (`out_of_scope_findings`, "noted, not filed"): ESCALATE to the seat. The card's Expected names every person and import write, and its first repro is a value stored "while no order exists", which a create reproduces exactly: a person's `POST` with a summary value is still stored until the first child write. The update lock is therefore not parity with `readonly: true`, which strips on insert too. Leaving insert alone is consistent with the #6014 note and is the area's route (6943935029), not a maintainer ruling. The PR body says `Fixes #34672`, so landing closes the card with that half open. The insert half needs its own card, with the maintainer deciding whether the #6014 note stands, before the Tier H step; no change to this head is needed for that.
- Dogfood battery: the claim says the PR owes the battery pinned to its head. The evidence is the lane's own run on `65f7837f`; the head differs from it by `packages/rest/src/rest-data-blank-typed-value.test.ts` alone (I confirmed the one-file delta in git), and the CI dogfood shards are skipped on this head. I accept the one-test-file delta as immaterial to the dogfood package; the seat should know the battery is not a check-run verdict on this head.
- Deviation, opened before #34709 landed: answered by the lane's merge-tree note; not re-derived here. Whichever lands second re-merges.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; `summaryFieldsLockedOnUpdate` is a walk of the in-memory field map.
- Spec prose outside the diff, follow-up only: the `onFieldsDropped` docblock in `packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts` and the `readonly` key's description list what the `readonly` reason covers and do not name a summary on update.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away. Read on `main`: `COMPUTED_VALUE_TYPES` declares `summary` never client-written; the only caller-supplied summary value the tree declares as supported is the initial value on insert (the #6014 note on `RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES`), which this diff leaves alone and pins. The Console and the import template already treat the type as non-writable. Nothing on `main` declares a person's update of a roll-up as a capability; the comment on `stripComputedWriteFields` records it as measured behaviour and "a separate question".

The placement is sound. Putting the lock in the one view all five update-side passes read means the hook view, the `readonlyWhen` record view, the stored row and the preview cannot disagree about the column. Using the static `readonly` strip instead of the `computed` door is what keeps the recompute's own write: that door runs in every context. Reusing reason `readonly` follows the `autonumber` precedent and adds no vocabulary.

Attempts to break it, and what I found:

- A system writer that loses its write: none. Recompute, enable refresh, backfill and the seed loader all write under `isSystem`.
- A schema-shape dependency: the view now returns a fresh `{ name, fields }` object whenever the object has a roll-up. The consumers read `name` and `fields` only, and the organization branch already returned that shape on main.
- An explicit `readonly: false` on a summary is locked too. Intended by the card ("whether or not"), and `readonly` defaults to `false`, so the two spellings were never distinguishable.

N1 (nit) — prose faces. The changeset and the `fields.mdx` paragraph say an update drops the value and name `isSystem` as the one exemption. Three statements are missing: (a) a historical import (`treatAsHistorical`, hence `preserveAudit`) in update mode keeps a supplied summary value, as it keeps any business read-only value; (b) an upsert import drops it on rows it updates and keeps it on rows it creates; (c) undoing an import committed before this release restores its `before` snapshot through an ordinary update (`data-action-routes.ts`, the undo door), so a summary value that import overwrote is not put back by the undo and stays until the next child write. I read (c) in the code and did not trace whether the undo answer reports the dropped key. Fixable in the changeset and the docs page.

N2 (nit) — the lock keys on `type === 'summary'` alone, while the roll-up index (`getSummaryDescriptors`) also needs `summaryOperations` and a resolvable child relation. A summary the engine has no descriptor for is locked on update although nothing recomputes it, so "the next child write replaces it" does not hold for that field. Lint already reports a summary without `summaryOperations` as incomplete, so no working declaration is affected. Leave as an accepted deviation.

N3 (nit) — `engine-validate.ts` calls `updateStaticReadonlySubject` once per row, so a preview over an object with roll-ups now copies the field map per row where it returned the schema itself. Small beside the strip's own walk of the same map. Leave as an accepted deviation.

### ① Derived judgments

The delta changes no accept-set and no public surface. It adds five statements to the narrowing's published text. Each is checked against the code at this head.

- **Upsert import: dropped on the rows it updates, kept on the rows it creates. TRUE.** `import-runner.ts` sends a matched row through `p.updateData` (line 1663) and an unmatched row through `p.createData` (line 1689) under one `writeCtx`. The update takes the lock, and the insert path is untouched.
- **A historical import keeps a summary value on update. TRUE.** The import writes with `preserveAudit: true` when `treatAsHistorical` is set (`import-runner.ts:1135`). Both update strips pass `preserveAudit` to `stripReadonlyFields` (`engine-update.ts:1474`, `:1866`), and `isPreservableUnderAudit` keeps any field that is not `system: true` (`rule-validator.ts:2877`). The synthesized `readonly: true` does not set `system`.
- **"And so does the undo of such an import" (changeset). TRUE.** `importUndoWriteContext` adds `preserveAudit: true` for a `treat_as_historical` job, for every caller (`data-action-routes.ts:291-297`).
- **Undoing an ordinary import restores through an ordinary update, so the summary value is not put back. TRUE.** The undo sends `u.before` through `p.updateData` with that context (`data-action-routes.ts:1048`). `captureBefore` keys the snapshot on the import's payload keys (`import-runner.ts:898-900`), so a summary column that an older import sent is in the snapshot, and the lock drops it on the restore. One case the sentence does not name: an in-process caller that undoes as the system principal writes under `isSystem`, so its restore is kept. "Ordinary" covers it, and no HTTP caller is the system principal.
- **"Committed before this release" (changeset) and "before this rule" (docs). Same set, neither false.** Only an import committed before the lock could have overwritten a summary.
- **"It stays until the next child write recomputes it."** True for a summary the engine has a descriptor for. L2's N2 (a summary without a descriptor is locked but never recomputed) applies to this sentence as it does to the earlier ones.

#### The escalation: is seat 2's scoping of the insert half (6948112119) sound?

**Short answer: the scope is sound, one of its two reasons is not, and one thing is owed before landing. It is not a finding on this head.**

What I verified in the code at this head:

1. **The hole is real and it is the card's own first repro.** A signed-in person's `POST` (or an import in `insert` mode, or the create rows of an upsert) that carries a value for a summary field without `readonly: true` stores that value. `initializeSummaryFields` skips a field the caller supplied (`engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts:491-503`), `RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES` holds only `autonumber`, and the PR's own test pins it ("insert keeps a caller's initial value"). The card's first repro is "the stored value is 90 while no order exists". A create reproduces exactly that state, and on a record that never gets a child write the value never heals.
2. **The card's Expected does cover it.** It reads "read-only for every person and import write". So the scope note's sentence "not a gap in this card" is wrong as written. It is a gap in the card's Expected, left open on purpose.
3. **Changing it does overturn a standing design statement, so it cannot be done under this card.** The #6014 note (`rule-validator.ts:1867-1899`) says in words that supplying an initial summary value is "a SUPPORTED authoring path", and names "a plain (non-`isSystem`, non-`preserveAudit`) import of a parent carrying `task_count: 42`" as the case to protect. It also warns that a naive strip stores `null`, because the seed pass has already skipped the field. That is a declared capability on `main`. Taking it away is a second narrowing with its own design (strip and re-seed, or refuse), its own BREAKING changeset and a maintainer ruling. This part of the seat's reasoning holds.
4. **A fact the ruling should have, which neither the seat nor L2 states.** The two beneficiaries the note and the PR prose name, seed data and historical imports, no longer need the carve-out. The seed loader writes under `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT`, which is `isSystem: true` (`execution-context.zod.ts:829`). A historical import is refused for every caller but the system principal (`importControlOptOutRefusal`, `import-prepare.ts:431`, #24348). The system principal passes every create-side strip. So the only caller the insert carve-out still serves is an ordinary signed-in person or an ordinary import, which is the card's actor. The case for keeping #6014 as it stands is weaker than the scope note says.

Against the two tests the seat asked for:

- **Does landing the update half leave a false answer?** Not in the product. The changeset and the docs page both say in plain words that a create keeps a sent value, and the code agrees. It would leave a false answer on the board: `Fixes #34672` closes a card whose Expected is half met, and the scope note makes the insert card conditional ("if it is wanted"). No insert card exists today (searched). After the merge the open half would live only in a closed PR's notes.
- **Does it leave a security hole the card promised to close?** It closes every write the card measured (all three repros are a `PATCH` or an import update). It leaves the create door, which the card's Expected names in words but did not measure. That door is not opened or widened by this PR, the declared mitigation works on it today (`readonly: true` is stripped on a non-system create, `isSystem` being the create strip's only exemption), and the card says the app is already adding `readonly: true`.

**So it is a separate gap that needs its own card, and it is not an S item on this PR.** The diff is correct and complete for what it claims, and no change to this head would close the gap.
